name: Cable Beach
tagline: The twenty-two kilometre beach, and the sunset camels
description: The resort side of Broome, west of the centre, built behind a beach that runs twenty-two kilometres of white sand into turquoise water. The sunset with camel trains along the sand is the town's defining image. Accommodation is resorts and holiday apartments, and prices swing hard between the dry and the wet.
bestFor: Stays where the beach is the entire point
pros: One of the great beaches in Australia at the door
Quiet and green compared with the town
cons: The highest prices in Broome during the dry
Fifteen minutes from Chinatown and the shops
Stingers and crocodile warnings apply in the wet

name: Chinatown
tagline: The old pearling quarter and the town's commercial centre
description: Broome's historic centre, where the pearling masters' shops and the corrugated-iron verandas survive along Carnarvon Street, now holding the pearl showrooms, the banks, the supermarkets and Sun Pictures, the oldest operating outdoor cinema in the world. This is where the practical business of the town happens.
bestFor: Anyone who needs shops, banks and the airport within a short distance
pros: All services, shops and the market close by
Sun Pictures and the pearling heritage
Airport is a few minutes away
cons: Hot and shadeless in the middle of the day
Quiet in the evening once the shops close

name: Old Broome and Town Beach
tagline: Between the two, with the mudflats and the Staircase to the Moon
description: The residential quarter between Chinatown and Roebuck Bay, with older houses under mango trees, the Town Beach on the bay side and the mangroves and mudflats beyond. This is where the Staircase to the Moon is watched, when the full moon rises over the exposed flats at low tide between March and October.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a real neighbourhood and the bay side of town
pros: Staircase to the Moon viewing and the night markets
cons: Town Beach is mudflat rather than sand
Crocodiles are present in Roebuck Bay

name: Bilingurr and the Northern Suburbs
tagline: Ordinary Broome, where the residents live
description: The residential estates spreading north from Cable Beach Road, with family houses, schools and the everyday services that the resorts do not provide. It is unremarkable to look at and it is where rents come down to something a long stay can absorb, with the beach still ten minutes away by car or bike.
bestFor: Long stays where the dry season rents elsewhere are prohibitive
pros: Ten minutes to Cable Beach by bike
A year-round community rather than a seasonal one
cons: A car or bicycle is necessary

name: Dampier Peninsula (up to 200 km north)
tagline: The red road north through Aboriginal community country
description: The peninsula running north from Broome, red pindan road through country belonging to Bardi Jawi and other communities, with Cape Leveque's red cliffs against white sand at the tip. Accommodation is community-run camps and lodges. Access requires permits for some areas and a four-wheel drive for much of it.
bestFor: Short stays on country rather than a base, arranged through the communities
pros: Some of the most striking coastline in Australia
Community-run tourism on the communities' own terms
cons: Up to three hours from Broome on unsealed road
Permits required for parts of it and a four-wheel drive for most
